_comment: Round 61 (R257): what every SDK's pending sign-offs helper answers for a feed. Each case is a feed, in order, written as abstract events that each SDK's test turns into its own served events (CloudEvent envelope, data.entry, data.deleted, sequence and hashes as its other feed tests build them). An event is {kind, entry, deleted}: kind is the feed kind; entry is the event's entry (null for a null entry), where a run.sealed entry is {run_id, signoff_required} and a run.deleted entry is {run_id}; deleted is null or {run_id} for a tombstone served in place of an entry. expected_pending lists the run ids the helper returns, in feed order, or expected_error is true when the helper must refuse the feed. The server keeps a run.sealed event's own entry even after the run is deleted; only an event whose entry is the deleted record itself (a refused, halted or failed run's receipt event) is served with a null entry and its tombstone. Sign-off events are covered by each SDK's own tests and the shared decision-in-force definition, not here.

cases.name: a run whose rule requires a sign-off is pending
a run whose rule requires no sign-off is not pending
a deleted run is left out once its run.deleted event appears
a run.deleted event before the run.sealed event also leaves the run out
a run.sealed event with a null entry is refused, even beside a tombstone
a run.sealed event with a null entry and no tombstone is refused
a run.sealed event naming run 0 is refused
a deleted refused run's receipt event and account changes are passed over
